Source code of utils.initialize_language:
```{python}
import functools

all_phrases, t_list = None, None
global phrases_per_section_list, phrases_per_section_list_org, regex_per_section
```

Declares global variables: phrases_per_section_list, phrases_per_section_list_org, regex_per_section

```{python}
phrases_file = "assets/all_phr.json"
with open(phrases_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        all_phrases = json.load(f)
```

The `all_phr.json` file contains standardized echocardiogram report phrases organized by anatomical structures and clinical findings. It's a comprehensive template library that maps cardiac assessment categories to their corresponding clinical descriptions. 


```{json}
{
  "Anatomical Structure": {
    "Measurement/Finding Category": [
      "Phrase 1",
      "Phrase 2",
      ...
    ]
  }
}
```


Opens file in JSON format and loads its content into the variable all_phrases

```{python}
all_phrases
```


```{python}
t_list = {k: [all_phrases[k][j] for j in all_phrases[k]] for k in all_phrases}
```

The line extracts phrase lists from the nested dictionary structure for each section. 

For example, it extracts all the phrases related to `"Left Ventricle"` and stores them in `t_list` under the same key. For the key `"Left Ventricle"`, t_list will contain a list of all phrases associated with that section, such as `"Left ventricle not well visualized."`, `"Left ventricle is grossly normal in size and systolic function."`, `"Left ventricle is normal in size and systolic function."`, `"The left ventricle is small by linear cavity dimension."`




```{python}
phrases_per_section_list = {
    k: functools.reduce(lambda a, b: a + b, v) for (k, v) in t_list.items()
}

phrases_per_section_list_org = {
    k: functools.reduce(lambda a, b: a + b, v) for (k, v) in t_list.items()
}
```

The code flattens nested lists of phrases for each section into single lists using `functools.reduce`.

For example, 
```{python}
# Before (t_list structure - nested lists)
"Left Ventricle": [
    ["Left ventricle not well visualized."],
    ["Normal LV size.", "Dilated LV."],
    ["Normal wall thickness.", "Mild hypertrophy."]
]

# After (phrases_per_section_list - flat list)
"Left Ventricle": [
    "Left ventricle not well visualized.",
    "Normal LV size.",
    "Dilated LV.",
    "Normal wall thickness.",
    "Mild hypertrophy."
]
```

Summary:
- The code initializes language-specific phrases for different sections by loading them from a JSON file.
- It flattens nested lists of phrases into single lists for easier processing (`phrases_per_section_list` and `phrases_per_section_list_org`).
- It converts these phrases into regex patterns to facilitate text matching later on (`regex_per_section`).


```{python}
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
```

Device agnostic code setup for PyTorch to use GPU if available, otherwise CPU.

```{python}
checkpoint = torch.load("model_data/weights/echo_prime_encoder.pt", map_location=device)
```

checkpoint is an OrderedDict from the collections module 


```{python}
echo_encoder = torchvision.models.video.mvit_v2_s() 
echo_encoder.head[-1] = torch.nn.Linear(echo_encoder.head[-1].in_features, 512)
echo_encoder.load_state_dict(checkpoint)
echo_encoder.eval() # Set the model in evaluation mode
echo_encoder.to(device)
for param in echo_encoder.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False
```

Constructs a small MViTV2 architecture and loads the pre-trained weights from the checkpoint. The model is set to evaluation mode, moved to the appropriate device (CPU or GPU), and all parameters are frozen to prevent further training.


```{python}
vc_state_dict = torch.load("model_data/weights/view_classifier.pt")
view_classifier = torchvision.models.convnext_base()
view_classifier.classifier[-1] = torch.nn.Linear(
    view_classifier.classifier[-1].in_features, 11
)
view_classifier.load_state_dict(vc_state_dict)

view_classifier.to(device)
view_classifier.eval()
for param in view_classifier.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False
```

Constructs a ConvNeXt base architecture for view classification, loads pre-trained weights, sets the model to evaluation mode, moves it to the appropriate device, and removes gradients from all parameters to prevent further training.
